h2: Jaguar XJ AJ-V8|Timing Chain Tensioner Issue?|
description: If your XJ is fitted with the 5.0L AJ133/AJ-V8 Gen III engine, particularly a 2012-2014 model, this is a genuinely well-documented design flaw - a hardened steel tensioner piston wears against a softer aluminium guide button over time, which can fail with little to no warning. It's serious enough to have been the subject of a US class-action lawsuit covering this exact engine. We replace the chain, tensioners and guides as standard on every rebuild.

callout.title: A Well-Documented Issue
callout.body: AJD-V6 injector seal leaks and timing chain wear are widely documented across Jaguar specialist forums and official TSBs.

heroHook.title: Include In Hero Hook:
heroHook.body: Yes - both verified: AJD-V6 widely documented with multiple TSBs; M156 pre-2012 established Jaguar specialist pattern.

features.title: New Timing Chains
features.body: Replaced as standard (where worn or damaged)

features.title: Peace Of Mind
features.body: No hidden extras - just a stronger, longer-lasting engine
